study type: Cross-sectional analysis within a prospective birth cohort
exposure: Per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substances (PFNA, PFOA, PFOS, PFHxS, Me-PFOSA-AcOH)
Psychosocial stress (self-reported depression, stressful life events, perceived stress, food insecurity, financial strain)
cohort: The study participants were 497 pregnant women from a prospective birth cohort.
finding: An interquartile range increase in PFNA was associated with elevated CRH levels, and this relationship was stronger among women experiencing psychosocial stress.
cross-section timing: During the second trimester of pregnancy
